physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: In a region, the electric potential varies as V = 10 − 50x, where V is in volts and x in metres. The electric field in the region is:
physics.explanation: E = −dV/dx = −(−50) = +50 V/m, so the field is 50 N/C along +x (the direction in which V decreases). (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A conducting wire connects two charged metallic spheres A and B of radii r1 and r2 respectively. The distance between the spheres is very large compared to their radii. The ratio of electric fields (EA/EB) at the surfaces of spheres A and B will be:
physics.explanation: Connected spheres reach the same potential: q1/r1 = q2/r2. E = kq/r², so E ∝ 1/r and EA/EB = r2/r1. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A long straight wire of circular cross-section (radius a) carries a steady current I, uniformly distributed across the cross-section. The magnitude of the magnetic field at a distance a/2 from the axis of the wire will be:
physics.explanation: Inside a uniformly carrying wire, B = μ0Ir/(2πa²). At r = a/2, B = μ0I/(4πa). (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: The shape of the interference fringes in Young’s double-slit experiment, when the distance between the slit and the screen is very large as compared to the slit-separation, is nearly
physics.explanation: When the screen distance is much larger than the slit separation, the (hyperbolic) fringes are very nearly straight lines. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: An electromagnetic wave passes from vacuum into a dielectric medium with relative electrical permittivity (3/2) and relative magnetic permeability (8/3). Then, its
physics.optionA: wavelength is doubled and frequency remains unchanged.
physics.optionB: wavelength is doubled and frequency is halved.
physics.optionC: wavelength is halved and frequency remains unchanged.
physics.optionD: wavelength and frequency both will remain unchanged.
physics.explanation: n = √(εr μr) = √(3/2 × 8/3) = 2. Frequency is unchanged on entering a medium, and wavelength λ' = λ/n is halved. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: In a series LCR circuit, the voltage across the resistor, capacitor and inductor is 10 V each. If the capacitor is short circuited, the voltage across the inductor will be
physics.explanation: VR = VL = VC = 10 V means resonance with source voltage 10 V and R = XL. With C shorted, I = 10/(√2 R), so VL = I·XL = 10/√2 = 5√2 V. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Electromagnetic waves used in a diagnostic tool in medicine have a wavelength range
physics.explanation: X-rays (about 1 nm to 10⁻³ nm) are used as a diagnostic tool in medicine. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: The distance of closest approach of an alpha particle is d when it moves with a velocity v head-on towards the target nucleus. If the velocity of the alpha particle is halved, the new distance of closest approach will be:
physics.explanation: At closest approach, ½mv² = kZe·2e/d, so d ∝ 1/v². Halving the velocity makes d four times: 4d. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A concave lens of focal length 10 cm is cut into two identical plano-concave lenses. The focal length of each lens will be
physics.explanation: 1/f = (n−1)(1/R1 − 1/R2). Each plano-concave half keeps only one curved surface, so its power halves and focal length doubles to 20 cm. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText:
Four independent waves are expressed as:
(i) y1 = A1 sin ωt
(ii) y2 = A2 sin 2ωt
(iii) y3 = A3 cos ωt
(iv) y4 = A4 sin(ωt + π/3)
The interference between two of these waves is possible in:
physics.explanation: Sustained interference needs waves of the same frequency. Waves (i), (iii) and (iv) all have angular frequency ω, while (ii) has 2ω. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Two heaters rated (P1, V) and (P2, V) are connected in series across a dc source of V/2 volt. The power consumed by the combination will be:
physics.explanation: R1 = V²/P1 and R2 = V²/P2. Across V/2 in series, P = (V/2)²/(R1 + R2) = (V²/4)/[V²(1/P1 + 1/P2)] = P1P2/[4(P1 + P2)]. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText:
Assertion (A): All atoms have a net magnetic moment.
Reason (R): A current loop does not always behave as a magnetic dipole.
physics.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
physics.optionD: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
physics.explanation: Both statements are false. Diamagnetic atoms have zero net magnetic moment, and a current loop always behaves as a magnetic dipole. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
physics.questionText:
Assertion (A): If accelerated electrons are passed through a narrow slit, a diffraction pattern is observed.
Reason (R): Electrons behave as both particles and waves.
physics.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
physics.optionD: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
physics.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: electrons have a wave nature (de Broglie waves), so they diffract through a narrow slit. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText:
Assertion (A): The mass of a nucleus is less than the sum of the masses of the constituent nucleons.
Reason (R): Energy is absorbed when the nucleons are bound together to form a nucleus.
physics.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
physics.optionD: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
physics.explanation: The assertion is true: a nucleus has a mass defect. The reason is false: energy is released, not absorbed, when nucleons bind to form a nucleus. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText:
Assertion (A): In Bohr model of hydrogen atom, the energy levels are discrete and quantised.
Reason (R): In a hydrogen atom, the electrostatic force on the electron provides the necessary centripetal force for it to revolve around the nucleus.
physics.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
physics.optionD: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
physics.explanation: Both statements are true, but the reason does not explain the assertion. Discrete energy levels follow from quantisation of angular momentum (L = nh/2π), not just from the electrostatic force acting as centripetal force. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: In a region the electric field is given by E = 4x î N/C. The potential difference between points A (x = 1 m) and B (x = 3 m), (VA − VB), is:
physics.explanation: VA − VB = ∫ from A to B of E·dx = ∫₁³ 4x dx = 2(3² − 1²) = 16 V. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: In an unbiased p-n junction, at equilibrium, which of the following statements is true?
physics.optionA: Diffusion current is zero but drift current exists.
physics.optionB: Diffusion current exists but drift current is zero.
physics.optionC: Diffusion and drift currents are equal and opposite.
physics.optionD: Both the diffusion and drift currents exist but are unequal. 
physics.explanation: At equilibrium in an unbiased p-n junction, the diffusion current and drift current are equal and opposite, so the net current is zero. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A copper wire is stretched to increase its length by 1%. Then the change in its resistance is close to
physics.explanation: With volume constant, R = ρL²/V, so R ∝ L². A 1% increase in length gives about a 2% increase in resistance. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A concave lens of focal length 40 cm is coaxially in contact with two convex lenses, each of focal length 20 cm, on each side. The focal length of the combination is
physics.explanation: 1/F = 1/20 + 1/20 − 1/40 = 3/40, so F = 40/3 cm (converging). (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: The distance-of-closest-approach for an alpha particle is ‘d’ when it moves head-on with speed v towards a target nucleus. If the alpha particle is replaced by a proton moving with the same speed, the new distance-of-closest-approach will be
physics.explanation: d = k(Ze)q/(½mv²) ∝ q/m. For an alpha particle q/m = 2e/4u; for a proton it is e/u, twice as large. So d becomes 2d. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Electromagnetic waves used for purification of water are
physics.explanation: Ultraviolet rays kill germs and are used in water purifiers. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A straight conductor lies along the x-axis and carries a current of 10 A along +x. The magnetic field B due to a 1 cm segment of this conductor, centred at the origin, at the point (0, 1 m, 0) is:
physics.explanation: dB = (μ0/4π)I dl × r/r³ = 10⁻⁷ × 10 × 0.01/1² = 10⁻⁸ T = 10 nT. Direction î × ĵ = k̂. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: The angular width of interference fringes in Young’s double-slit experiment depends on
physics.optionA: distance between the slits and the screen only
physics.optionC: both wavelength of light used and the slits separation
physics.explanation: Angular fringe width θ = λ/d depends on the wavelength and the slit separation, not on the screen distance. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A resistor and an inductor of negligible resistance are connected in series to a 20 V ac source. If the voltage across the resistor is 12 V, the voltage across the inductor will be
physics.explanation: V² = VR² + VL², so VL = √(20² − 12²) = 16 V. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: The electric potential at points in the x-y plane is given by V = 1.0x² − 2.0y², where V is in volts and x, y are in metres. The angle that the electric field at point (2.0 m, 1.0 m) makes with the positive x-axis is:
physics.explanation: E = −∇V = (−2x)î + (4y)ĵ = −4î + 4ĵ at (2, 1). This vector points at 135° to the +x axis. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A current of 1.5 A is maintained in a copper wire of length 1 m and area of cross-section 1.7 × 10⁻⁷ m². The magnitude of the electric field in the wire is [ρCu = 1.7 × 10⁻⁸ Ω m]:

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Light from a small object in air falls on a convex spherical glass surface (n = 1.5) of radius of curvature R. A real image of the object will be formed if the object distance u is related to R as:
physics.explanation: For refraction from air (n = 1) to glass (1.5) at a convex surface: 1.5/v + 1/u = 0.5/R (with u the object distance in magnitude). v is positive (real image) only when u > 2R. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: The ratio of the potential energy to the kinetic energy of an electron in nth orbit of Bohr model of hydrogen atom is 1
physics.explanation: In a Bohr orbit, PE = −2KE, so PE/KE = −2. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Welders wear special glass goggles or face masks with glass windows to protect their eyes from
physics.explanation: Welding arcs produce intense ultraviolet radiation; special glass goggles protect the welder's eyes from UV. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2025, 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: The phenomenon of interference is shown by
physics.explanation: Interference is a property of all waves — longitudinal, transverse mechanical and electromagnetic. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Three point charges 2q, −2q and q are kept at the vertices of an equilateral triangle of side l. The potential energy of the system is:
physics.explanation: U = k[(2q)(−2q) + (−2q)(q) + (q)(2q)]/l = −4kq²/l = −q²/(πε0 l). (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Two metal spheres of radii r1 and r2 (> r1) having charges q1 and q2 respectively kept in air, are brought in contact. Which of the following statements is not correct?
physics.optionA: The total charge of the two spheres is conserved.
physics.optionB: Both spheres attain the same potential.
physics.optionC: The final potential of the system equals (1/4πε0)(q1 + q2)/(r1 + r2)
physics.optionD: The final potential of the system equals (1/4πε0)(q1 + q2)(r1 + r2)/(r1r2)
physics.explanation: After contact, the common potential is V = (q1 + q2)/[4πε0(r1 + r2)]. The expression with (r1 + r2)/(r1r2) is not correct. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
physics.questionText: The maximum kinetic energy of the electrons emitted from a photo sensitive surface depends on
physics.optionA: Work function of the surface φ0 only
physics.optionB: Frequency of the incident radiation ν only
physics.optionC: Intensity of the incident radiation I only
physics.explanation: Kmax = hν − φ0, so it depends on both the frequency of incident radiation and the work function, not on intensity. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: In Bohr model of hydrogen atom, for large values of n, the distance between the consecutive orbits is proportional to
physics.explanation: rn ∝ n², so the spacing between consecutive orbits r(n+1) − rn ∝ 2n + 1, which is proportional to n for large n. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A straight long wire lying along y-axis, carries a current of 1 A along –y direction. The magnetic field due to the conductor at a point (50 cm, 0, 0) will point along.
physics.explanation: dl is along −ĵ and r is along +î: (−ĵ) × î = +k̂. So the field at (50 cm, 0, 0) points along +z. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Which of the following materials has positive and small value of magnetic susceptibility?
physics.explanation: Paramagnetic materials such as aluminium have a small positive susceptibility. Cu and Bi are diamagnetic, and Ni is ferromagnetic (large χ). (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A galvanometer of resistance 27 Ω is converted into an ammeter of range 0–10 mA using a resistance of 3 Ω. The galvanometer will show full-scale deflection for a current of about:
physics.explanation: Ig·G = (I − Ig)S gives Ig = IS/(G + S) = 10 × 3/30 = 1 mA. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2024, 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: The magnetic flux φ (in Wb) linked with a coil is related to time t (in s) as φ = 5At² + Bt − 2C. The SI units of A and B are respectively:
physics.explanation: φ = 5At² + Bt − 2C. Each term is in Wb, so A is in Wb s⁻² and B in Wb s⁻¹. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A magnet held vertically, with its north pole down is dropped along the axis of a closed solenoid placed vertically on a table. If the observer looks down from the top,
physics.optionA: the induced current will flow in the anticlockwise direction.
physics.optionB: the induced current will flow in the clockwise direction.
physics.optionC: no induced current will flow in the solenoid.
physics.optionD: the magnet will fall with a constant velocity.
physics.explanation: As the north pole approaches, the top of the solenoid becomes a north pole to oppose it. Viewed from the top, this means anticlockwise current. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: An electromagnetic wave is propagating along the x-axis. At any instant, the phase difference (in radian) between the electric field E and the magnetic field B associated with the wave is:
physics.explanation: In an EM wave, E and B oscillate in phase, so the phase difference is zero. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
physics.questionText:
Assertion (A): On increasing the intensity of incident light of frequency ν (> ν0) on a photosensitive surface, the photocurrent increases.
Reason (R): The stopping potential for a photosensitive surface increases with increase of frequency ν (> ν0) of incident light.
physics.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
physics.optionD: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
physics.explanation: Both statements are true, but the reason does not explain the assertion. Photocurrent rises with intensity because more photons eject more electrons; the stopping potential depends on frequency, which is a separate fact. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText:
Assertion (A): On forward biasing a p-n junction diode, the height of the barrier potential increases.
Reason (R): In forward biasing of a p-n junction diode, the direction of the applied voltage is in the same direction as the built-in potential.
physics.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
physics.optionD: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
physics.explanation: Both statements are false. Forward bias lowers the barrier height, because the applied voltage opposes the built-in potential. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText:
Assertion (A): Light added to light can produce darkness.
Reason (R): When two coherent light waves interfere, there is darkness at position of destructive interference.
physics.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
physics.optionD: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
physics.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: at points of destructive interference of two coherent waves, the intensity is zero (darkness). (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText:
Assertion (A): Two electric heaters of power P1 and P2 (> P1) are joined in series across a dc source of voltage V. The power consumed by the combination will be less than that consumed by P1 when connected across the same source.
Reason (R): The power consumed by a electric device when connected to a dc source of voltage V is proportional to its resistance.
physics.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
physics.optionD: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
physics.explanation: The assertion is true: in series P = V²/(R1 + R2) < V²/R1. The reason is false: at constant V, P = V²/R is inversely proportional to resistance. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Three point charges +q, −2q and +q are placed along the x-axis at x = −1 m, x = 0 m and x = 2 m respectively. The potential energy of the system is:

physics.subject: Physics
physics.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
physics.questionText: A photosensitive surface is illuminated by radiations of wavelengths λ1, λ2 (> λ1) and λ3, one by one, and photoemission is observed in each case. λ1 and λ2 lie in the UV range and λ3 in the visible range. If V1, V2 and V3 are the stopping potentials in these cases respectively, then:
physics.explanation: eV0 = hc/λ − φ0, so a shorter wavelength gives a larger stopping potential. λ1 < λ2 < λ3 gives V1 > V2 > V3. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: In Bohr model of hydrogen atom, the value of potential energy of an electron in nth orbit varies with ‘n’ as 1
physics.explanation: En ∝ 1/n² and PE = 2En, so the potential energy varies as 1/n². (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: In the Bohr model of hydrogen atom, an electron makes a transition from n = 4 to n = 1 and a photon of frequency ν is emitted. The frequency of the photon emitted when an electron makes a transition from n = 4 to n = 2 in the same model is:
physics.explanation: ν ∝ (1/n1² − 1/n2²). For 4→1 this is 15/16; for 4→2 it is 3/16. The ratio is 1/5, so the frequency is ν/5. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A magnet is dropped through a small conducting loop which has a small cut in it. Which of the following statements is correct?
physics.optionA: The speed of the falling magnet increases as it approaches the loop and starts decreasing as it crosses the loop.
physics.optionB: Acceleration of magnet increases as it approaches the loop and starts decreasing as it crosses the loop.
physics.optionC: Speed of magnet remains uniform as it moves through the loop.
physics.optionD: Acceleration of the magnet remains uniform as it moves through the loop.
physics.explanation: With a cut in the loop no current flows, so there is no opposing force. The magnet falls with uniform acceleration g. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText:
The magnetic fields associated with four electromagnetic waves are given below:
I. B1 = (4 × 10⁻⁶ T) sin[0.7 × 10³x + 1.4 × 10¹¹t]
II. B2 = (2 × 10⁻⁷ T) sin[0.6 × 10³x + 1.5 × 10¹¹t]
III. B3 = (3 × 10⁻⁵ T) sin[0.5 × 10³x + 1.5 × 10¹¹t]
IV. B4 = (5 × 10⁻⁴ T) sin[0.2 × 10⁴x + 4.8 × 10¹¹t]
Which wave is travelling in free space?
physics.explanation: Wave speed = ω/k. For III, (1.5 × 10¹¹)/(0.5 × 10³) = 3 × 10⁸ m/s = c, so III travels in free space. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Which of the following substances has relative magnetic permeability μr >> 1?
physics.explanation: Ferromagnetic nickel has μr >> 1. Al is paramagnetic (μr slightly > 1), and Cu and Pb are diamagnetic. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2024, 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A straight conductor lies along x-axis and carries a current of 2 A along +x direction. The magnetic field at a point (0, 40 cm, 0) due to 1 cm length of conductor centered at the origin points along.
physics.explanation: dl is along +x and r is along +y: î × ĵ = k̂, so the field is along the z-axis. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A person is standing facing geographic north and a vertical wire in front of him is carrying a current in downward direction. The direction of magnetic field at a point on the right side of wire is
physics.explanation: Take east = +x, north = +y, up = +z. dl = −k̂ and the point lies to the east (+x): (−k̂) × î = −ĵ, i.e. south. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Which one of the following materials has magnetic susceptibility χ in the range −1 < χ < 0?
physics.explanation: Diamagnetic materials have −1 < χ < 0; copper is diamagnetic. Al and copper chloride are paramagnetic, and Ni is ferromagnetic. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Two identical circular loops A and B of metal wire are arranged on a table close to each other. Loop A is connected to a battery and the current in it increases with time. In response, the loop B
physics.optionD: rotates about its centre of mass which is fixed
physics.explanation: An increasing current in A induces an opposite current in B. Opposite currents repel, so B is repelled. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: In Bohr model of hydrogen atom, an electron is moving in an orbit, with total energy –3.4 eV. Its angular momentum will be
physics.explanation: E = −3.4 eV corresponds to n = 2, so L = 2h/2π = h/π = 2.1 × 10⁻³⁴ J s. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: According to Bohr model of hydrogen atom, the time period of an electron in its nth orbit is proportional to
physics.explanation: T = 2πr/v with r ∝ n² and v ∝ 1/n, so T ∝ n³. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
physics.questionText: The equivalent mass of a photon of wavelength 100 nm is
physics.explanation: m = h/(cλ) = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴/(3 × 10⁸ × 10⁻⁷) = 2.21 × 10⁻³⁵ kg. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A particle of mass m and charge q starts from rest and moves in an electric field E = E0 î. After travelling a distance x in the field along the x-axis, the kinetic energy of the particle will be:
physics.explanation: Work done by the field = force × distance = qE0x, which equals the kinetic energy gained from rest. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A plane electromagnetic wave travels through a medium and the magnetic field associated with it is given by B = 5 × 10⁻⁸ sin(3 × 10¹⁰t − 150x) T, where x is in metres and t in seconds. The velocity of the wave is:
physics.explanation: v = ω/k = (3 × 10¹⁰)/150 = 2.0 × 10⁸ m/s. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A thin plano-convex lens and a thin equi-concave lens are kept coaxially in contact. Both lenses are made of glass of refractive index μ, and R is the radius of curvature of each curved surface. The focal length of the combination is:
physics.explanation: Plano-convex: 1/f1 = (μ−1)/R. Equi-concave: 1/f2 = −2(μ−1)/R. Sum: 1/F = −(μ−1)/R, so F = −R/(μ−1). (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: The phase difference between the two superimposing waves that give rise to a bright spot in a Young’s double-slit experiment is (n is an integer) : 
physics.explanation: Constructive interference (bright fringe) occurs when the phase difference is 2nπ. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A telescope has an objective lens of focal length 144 cm and an eyepiece of focal length 6·0 cm. The magnifying power and the length of telescope tube will be respectively:
physics.explanation: Normal adjustment: M = fo/fe = 144/6 = 24, and tube length L = fo + fe = 150 cm. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: In which of the following, total internal reflection does not occur?
physics.explanation: Twinkling of stars is due to atmospheric refraction (fluctuating refractive index), not total internal reflection. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
physics.questionText: A proton and an alpha particle have equal momentum. The ratio of their kinetic energies (Ep/Eα) and of their de Broglie wavelengths (λp/λα) are respectively:
physics.explanation: K = p²/2m: with equal p, Kp/Kα = mα/mp = 4. λ = h/p is the same for both, so the ratio is 1. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: The process named ‘minority carrier injection’ in a p-n junction diode occurs during:
physics.explanation: Under forward bias, holes are injected into the n-side and electrons into the p-side, where they are minority carriers — minority carrier injection. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText:
Assertion (A): In a Wheatstone bridge circuit, if we interchange the positions of the cell and the galvanometer, the balance condition P/Q = R/S remains unchanged.
Reason (R): P/Q = R/S ⇒ P/R = Q/S, so the balance condition remains the same.
physics.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
physics.optionD: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
physics.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: P/Q = R/S is equivalent to P/R = Q/S, so interchanging the cell and galvanometer leaves the balance condition unchanged. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText:
Assertion (A): The cylindrical soft iron core in a moving coil galvanometer only makes the magnetic field radial and does not affect the strength of the magnetic field.
Reason (R): In a moving coil galvanometer, the plane of the coil is always perpendicular to the magnetic field.
physics.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
physics.optionD: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
physics.explanation: Both statements are false. The soft iron core both makes the field radial and increases its strength, and in a radial field the plane of the coil is always parallel to the field. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
physics.questionText:
Assertion (A): Photoelectric current depends upon the intensity of the incident radiation.
Reason (R): Stopping potential is independent of the intensity of the incident radiation.
physics.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
physics.optionD: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
physics.explanation: Both statements are true, but the reason does not explain the assertion. Photocurrent depends on intensity (number of photons); stopping potential depends only on frequency. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2024, 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText:
Assertion (A): Nuclear forces are always attractive.
Reason (R): The nuclear force between protons and neutrons in a nucleus is a weak force.
physics.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
physics.optionD: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
physics.explanation: Both statements are false. The nuclear force is repulsive at very short distances (below about 0.8 fm), and it is the strongest force, not a weak one. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2025, 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: An equiconvex lens of focal length 15 cm is cut into two equal plano-convex halves. The focal length of each half will be:
physics.explanation: Cutting perpendicular to the axis leaves each half with one curved surface, so its power halves and f doubles to 30 cm. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: An electric dipole p = 2qa î is placed in the x-y plane, centred at the origin. Let E1 and E2 be the magnitudes of the electric field at a point at distance r (>> a) from its centre, along its axis and on its equatorial plane respectively. Then E1/E2 is:
physics.explanation: For r >> a, E_axial = 2kp/r³ and E_equatorial = kp/r³, so E1/E2 = 2. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A plano-convex lens, made of glass (n = 1·5) has a curved surface whose radius is 40 cm. The image formed of an object is of the same size as that of the object. The distance of the object from the lens is:
physics.explanation: f = R/(n−1) = 40/0.5 = 80 cm. A same-size real image forms when u = 2f = 160 cm. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A metallic rod of 1 m length is rotated with a frequency of 40 rev/s, with one end hinged at the centre and the other end at the circumference of a circular metallic ring of radius 1 m, about an axis passing through the centre and perpendicular to the plane of the ring. A constant and uniform magnetic field of 0·5 T parallel to the axis is present in the region. The value of emf induced between the centre and the metallic ring is close to:
physics.explanation: e = ½BωL² = ½ × 0.5 × (2π × 40) × 1² ≈ 62.8 V ≈ 63 V. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
physics.questionText: The velocity of the photoelectrons emitted from a surface depends upon the:
physics.optionC: Work function of the surface only
physics.optionD: Both wavelength of the incident radiation and work function of the surface
physics.explanation: ½mv²max = hc/λ − φ0, so the speed depends on both the wavelength of incident radiation and the work function. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A ray of monochromatic light travelling in air is incident on a glass slab and is partly reflected and partly refracted. Both the reflected and refracted lights will have:
physics.explanation: Frequency is set by the source and stays the same on reflection and refraction; wavelength and speed change in the denser medium. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A square loop of side L lies in the x-y plane in a magnetic field B = B0(2î + 3ĵ + 4k̂), where B0 is a constant. The magnetic flux through the loop is:
physics.explanation: For a loop in the x-y plane, A = L²k̂, so φ = B·A = 4B0L². (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A ray of yellow light undergoes total internal reflection when it is incident at the interface of two media. This ray is successively replaced by the ray of blue, green and red lights. Which of the following statements is true if the angle of incidence is same in all cases?
physics.optionA: Total internal reflection occurs for blue light only.
physics.optionB: Total internal reflection occurs for red light only.
physics.optionC: Total internal reflection occurs for both green and blue lights.
physics.optionD: None of them will undergo total internal reflection.
physics.explanation: Critical angle decreases as refractive index increases (blue > green > yellow > red). Light with a smaller critical angle than yellow — green and blue — will also undergo TIR. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Two wires of the same length and same area of cross-section, but made of different materials of resistivities ρ1 and ρ2, are connected in series. The equivalent resistivity of the combination is:
physics.explanation: In series, R = ρ1L/A + ρ2L/A = ρeq(2L)/A, so ρeq = (ρ1 + ρ2)/2. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: An electron moves around the nucleus in a circular orbit of radius r and makes n revolutions per second. The value of equivalent current in the orbit is : e
physics.explanation: Charge e passes any point n times per second, so I = ne. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: The dimensions of the rate of change of magnetic flux are:
physics.explanation: dφ/dt = emf (volt) = W/A, with dimensions [M L² T⁻³ A⁻¹]. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: An ac voltage is given as v = 14 sin (314t) V. The average and the effective value of the voltage (in V) over a cycle are respectively:
physics.explanation: The average of a sinusoid over a full cycle is 0. Vrms = 14/√2 ≈ 10 V. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: The ratio of amplitude of electric field to the amplitude of the magnetic field associated with an electromagnetic wave propagating in glass (n = 1·5) is:
physics.explanation: E0/B0 = v = c/n = (3 × 10⁸)/1.5 = 2 × 10⁸ m/s. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
physics.questionText: While studying photoelectric emission from a given surface, the wavelength of the incident radiation is changed from 600 nm to 400 nm, keeping the intensity of radiation the same. Then:
physics.explanation: Decreasing the wavelength increases photon energy, so the maximum KE and cut-off (stopping) potential increase. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
physics.questionText: Radiation of wavelength 331 nm irradiates the following metals: Na (work function 1.92 eV), K (2.15 eV), Ca (3.20 eV) and Mo (4.17 eV). Which of the following statements is correct?
physics.optionA: Only Na and K show photoelectric emission.
physics.optionB: Only Mo will not show photoelectric emission.
physics.optionC: All of the given metals show photoelectric emission.
physics.optionD: None of them show photoelectric emission.
physics.explanation: E = 1240/331 ≈ 3.75 eV, which exceeds the work functions of Na, K and Ca but not Mo (4.17 eV). Only Mo shows no emission. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
physics.questionText: The kinetic energy of a charged particle is increased to four times of its initial value. The de Broglie wavelength associated with the particle will:
physics.optionA: increase by 100% of its initial value.
physics.optionB: increase by 50% of its initial value.
physics.optionC: decrease by 25% of its initial value.
physics.optionD: decrease by 50% of its initial value.
physics.explanation: λ = h/√(2mK), so if K becomes 4 times, λ halves — a 50% decrease. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Paschen series in spectrum of hydrogen atom lies in:
physics.optionD: partly in ultraviolet region and partly in visible region
physics.explanation: The Paschen series (transitions to n = 3) lies in the infrared region. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: In a reversed-biased p-n junction diode, the applied voltage mostly drops across:
physics.explanation: In reverse bias, the high-resistance depletion region takes almost all the applied voltage. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText:
Assertion (A): The work done, in taking a unit charge around a closed loop of an electric circuit involving cells and resistors in the loop, is zero.
Reason (R): The potential at a point depends on the location of the point in the loop. After completing one round, the charge comes back to the point of start.
physics.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
physics.optionD: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
physics.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: potential is a function of position, so after a full loop the net potential change, and hence work per unit charge, is zero. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText:
Assertion (A): When a ferromagnetic substance is heated to high temperature it becomes paramagnetic in nature.
Reason (R): The disappearance of magnetisation of a ferromagnet is abrupt and not gradual.
physics.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
physics.optionD: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
physics.explanation: The assertion is true: above the Curie temperature a ferromagnet becomes paramagnetic. The reason is false: the disappearance of magnetisation with temperature is gradual, not abrupt. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText:
Assertion (A): When a convex lens made of glass is immersed in water, its converging power increases.
Reason (R): The focal length of a lens depends only on the radii of curvature of its two faces.
physics.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
physics.optionD: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
physics.explanation: Both statements are false. In water, (nrel − 1) falls, so the converging power decreases, and focal length depends on the refractive index as well as the radii. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText:
Assertion (A): The conductivity of an n-type semiconductor is higher than that of a p-type semiconductor at a given temperature.
Reason (R): The electrons being in the conduction band in n-type semiconductor are more mobile than the holes in the valence band in p-type semiconductor.
physics.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
physics.optionD: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
physics.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: electrons in the conduction band are more mobile than holes, so n-type has higher conductivity at the same doping. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A wire is gradually stretched to make it 100% longer. Its resistance will increase by:
physics.explanation: With volume constant, R ∝ L². Doubling L makes R four times, an increase of 300%. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A closely wound long solenoid of self-inductance L is cut into two identical solenoids. The value of self-inductance of each small solenoid will be : L
physics.explanation: L = μ0N²A/l. Each half has N/2 turns and length l/2, so L' = L/2. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Which of the following characteristics of electrons determines the current in the conductor?
physics.optionC: Both drift velocity and thermal velocity
physics.explanation: Current I = neAvd depends only on drift velocity; thermal velocities are random and average to zero. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A coil having 100 closely wound turns and area of cross-section 300 mm² carries a current of 5 mA. The magnitude of the magnetic moment associated with the coil is:
physics.explanation: m = NIA = 100 × 5 × 10⁻³ × 300 × 10⁻⁶ = 1.5 × 10⁻⁴ A m². (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
physics.questionText: In an experiment on photoelectric emission, the intensity of incident radiation is halved keeping its frequency constant. As a result:
physics.optionB: maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons will remain the same.
physics.explanation: Maximum kinetic energy and stopping potential depend only on frequency. Halving the intensity only reduces the photocurrent. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: The resistivity ρ of a metal increases with rise in temperature because:
physics.optionA: Only the relaxation time τ of electrons decreases with temperature.
physics.optionB: Only the number of electrons per unit volume n increases appreciably.
physics.optionC: τ decreases with temperature but n does not change appreciably.
physics.optionD: τ decreases with temperature and n increases.
physics.explanation: ρ = m/(ne²τ). In metals n is nearly constant with temperature, while relaxation time τ decreases due to more collisions, so ρ increases. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Two coils are placed closed to each other. The mutual inductance of the pair of coils depends upon the:
physics.optionA: rate at which currents change in the two coils.
physics.optionB: relative position and orientation of the coils.
physics.optionD: value of voltage induced in one coil due to change in value of current in the other coil.
physics.explanation: Mutual inductance depends on the geometry — the relative position and orientation of the coils (and medium) — not on currents or their rates of change. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Which of the following statements is true about mobility of charge carriers in a metal?
physics.optionA: Mobility increases with increase in applied electric field.
physics.optionB: Mobility decreases with increase in temperature.
physics.optionC: Mobility is independent of the mass of the charge carrier.
physics.optionD: Mobility increases with increase in temperature
physics.explanation: μ = eτ/m. As temperature rises, τ falls, so mobility decreases. It does not depend on the applied field. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A galvanometer of resistance G is converted into a voltmeter of range (0 − V) by connecting a resistor of 250 Ω with it. If the 250 Ω resistor is replaced by a 900 Ω resistor, its range becomes (0 − 3V). The resistance G of the galvanometer is:
physics.explanation: V = Ig(G + 250) and 3V = Ig(G + 900), so 3(G + 250) = G + 900 and G = 75 Ω. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: The magnetic flux through a loop placed in a magnetic field can be changed by changing:
physics.optionB: the value of magnetic field only
physics.optionC: orientation of the loop in the magnetic field only
physics.optionD: any one or more of the factors given in
physics.explanation: φ = BA cos θ, so it changes with any of B, A or orientation θ. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Which of the following statements is not true for electric energy in ac form compared to that in dc form?
physics.optionB: ac can be easily and efficiently converted from one voltage to the other.
physics.optionC: ac can be transmitted economically over long distances.
physics.explanation: AC is more dangerous than DC of the same voltage, so "ac is less dangerous" is not true. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
physics.questionText: Light of which of the following colours will have the maximum energy in a photon associated with it?
physics.explanation: E = hν; blue light has the highest frequency among these colours, so its photons have the most energy. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Nuclides with the same number of neutrons are called:
physics.explanation: Nuclides with the same neutron number are isotones; same Z are isotopes, and same A are isobars. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: The radius of a nucleus of mass number 125 is (R0 = 1.2 fm):

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: The energy of an electron in an orbit in hydrogen atom is – 3·4 eV. Its angular momentum in the orbit will be : 3h 2h
physics.explanation: E = −13.6/n² = −3.4 eV gives n = 2, so L = nh/2π = 2h/2π = h/π. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A good diode checked by a multimeter should indicate:
physics.optionA: high resistance in reverse bias and a low resistance in forward bias
physics.optionB: high resistance in both forward bias and reverse bias
physics.optionC: low resistance in both reverse bias and forward bias
physics.optionD: high resistance in forward bias and low resistance in reverse bias
physics.explanation: A good diode conducts in forward bias (low resistance) and blocks in reverse bias (high resistance). (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText:
Assertion (A): Induced emf produced in a coil will be more when the magnetic flux linked with the coil is more.
Reason (R): Induced emf produced is directly proportional to the magnetic flux.
physics.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
physics.optionD: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
physics.explanation: Both statements are false. Induced emf depends on the rate of change of magnetic flux, e = −dφ/dt, not on the flux itself. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText:
Assertion (A): In Young's double-slit experiment, the fringe width for dark and bright fringes is the same.
Reason (R): Fringe width is given by β = λD/d, where symbols have their usual meanings.
physics.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
physics.optionD: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
physics.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: β = λD/d is the same for bright and dark fringes. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText:
Assertion (A): Energy is released when heavy nuclei undergo fission or light nuclei undergo fusion.
Reason (R): For heavy nuclei, binding energy per nucleon increases with increasing Z while for light nuclei, it decreases with increasing Z.
physics.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
physics.optionD: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
physics.explanation: The assertion is true: fission and fusion both release energy. The reason is false: binding energy per nucleon increases with A for light nuclei and decreases with A for heavy nuclei. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
physics.questionText:
Assertion (A): Photoelectric effect is a spontaneous phenomenon.
Reason (R): According to the wave picture of radiation, an electron would take hours/days to absorb sufficient energy to overcome the work function and come out from a metal surface.
physics.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
physics.optionD: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
physics.explanation: Both statements are true, but the reason does not explain the assertion. The instantaneous emission is explained by the photon picture; the reason only states what the wave picture would predict. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: The rms and the average values of an ac voltage V = V0 sin ωt over a cycle will respectively be:
physics.explanation: For V = V0 sin ωt, Vrms = V0/√2 and the average over a full cycle is zero. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Two point charges −Q and Q are located at points (d, 0) and (0, d) respectively in the x-y plane. The electric field E at the origin will be:
physics.explanation: −Q at (d, 0) gives a field at the origin towards itself (+î); +Q at (0, d) gives a field away from itself (−ĵ). Each has magnitude kQ/d², so E = (1/4πε0)(Q/d²)(î − ĵ). (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: An electron is moving with velocity v0 î. If a uniform electric field E = E0 ĵ is set up in the region, the electron will:
physics.explanation: A constant force perpendicular to the initial velocity gives uniform acceleration in one direction and uniform velocity in the other — a parabolic path. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A charged particle of mass m having kinetic energy K passes undeflected through a region with electric field E and magnetic field B acting perpendicular to each other. The mass m of the particle will be:
physics.explanation: Undeflected motion needs qE = qvB, so v = E/B. Then K = ½mv² gives m = 2K/v² = 2KB²/E². (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: The energy of an electron revolving in the nth orbit in Bohr model of hydrogen atom is proportional to:
physics.explanation: En = −13.6/n² eV, so energy is proportional to 1/n². (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Consider the nuclear reaction X → Y + Z. Let Mx, My and Mz be the masses of the three nuclei X, Y and Z respectively. Then which of the following relations hold true?
physics.explanation: For a spontaneous decay X → Y + Z, energy (Q-value) is released, so Mx > My + Mz. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Two points R and S are equidistant from two charges +Q and −2Q. The work done in moving a charge −Q from point R to S is:
physics.explanation: R and S are equidistant from both charges, so they are at the same potential and the work done W = qΔV is zero. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: The potential difference across a cell in an open circuit is 8 V. It falls to 4 V when a current of 4 A is drawn from it. The internal resistance of the cell is:
physics.explanation: E = 8 V, V = 4 V at I = 4 A: r = (E − V)/I = 4/4 = 1 Ω. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A diamagnetic substance is brought near the north or south pole of a bar magnet. It will be:
physics.optionC: repelled by the north pole and attracted by the south pole.
physics.optionD: attracted by the north pole and repelled by the south pole.
physics.explanation: A diamagnetic substance is weakly repelled by both poles; it moves from stronger to weaker field regions. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A rectangular conductor PSRQ has a movable arm PQ placed in a magnetic field. The emf induced when PQ is moved with a velocity v does not depend on:
physics.explanation: The motional emf e = Blv depends on B, v and the length of PQ, not on the resistance of the circuit. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: The radius of the nth orbit in Bohr model of hydrogen atom is proportional to : 1
physics.explanation: rn = n²a0, so the radius is proportional to n². (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Hydrogen atom initially in the ground state, absorbs a photon which excites it to n = 5 level. The wavelength of the photon is:
physics.explanation: 1/λ = R(1 − 1/25) = 1.097 × 10⁷ × 24/25, so λ ≈ 95 nm (ultraviolet). (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: The mass density of a nucleus of mass number A is:
physics.explanation: R ∝ A^(1/3), so volume ∝ A and mass ∝ A. Nuclear density is independent of A. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: When an intrinsic semiconductor is doped with a small amount of trivalent impurity, then:
physics.optionC: there will be more free electrons than holes in the semiconductor.
physics.explanation: A trivalent (acceptor) impurity creates holes and makes the semiconductor p-type, with more holes than electrons. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText:
Assertion (A): When a bar of copper is placed in an external magnetic field, the field lines get concentrated inside the bar.
Reason (R): Copper is a paramagnetic substance.
physics.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
physics.optionD: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
physics.explanation: Both statements are false. Copper is diamagnetic, so field lines are expelled from (not concentrated inside) the bar. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText:
Assertion (A): The phase difference between any two points on a wavefront is zero.
Reason (R): All points on a wavefront are at the same distance from the source and thus oscillate in the same phase.
physics.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
physics.optionD: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
physics.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: a wavefront is the locus of points oscillating in phase, so the phase difference between any two points on it is zero. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
physics.questionText:
Assertion (A): Photoelectric effect demonstrates the particle nature of light.
Reason (R): Photoelectric current is proportional to intensity of incident radiation for frequencies more than the threshold frequency.
physics.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
physics.optionD: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
physics.explanation: Both statements are true, but the reason does not explain the assertion. Particle nature is shown by instantaneous emission and Kmax depending on frequency; dependence of current on intensity does not demonstrate it. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023, 2026)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Two identical circular coaxial coils A and B, arranged in vertical planes parallel to each other, carry currents in the same direction. If the distance between the coils is decreased at a constant rate, the current:
physics.optionA: increases in A and decreases in B.
physics.optionB: decreases in both A and B.
physics.optionC: increases in both A and B.
physics.optionD: remains same in both A and B.
physics.explanation: As the coils approach, the flux through each increases. Induced currents oppose this increase, so the current decreases in both A and B. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: The minimum distance between an object and its real image formed by a convex lens of focal length f is:
physics.explanation: The object-real image distance (u + v) is minimum when u = v = 2f, giving 4f. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
physics.questionText: A photon of energy 7 eV is incident on a metal surface having a work function of 3.75 eV. The stopping potential is:
physics.explanation: eV0 = E − φ0 = 7 − 3.75 = 3.25 eV, so the stopping potential is 3.25 V. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: The atomic number of an atom represents:
physics.optionB: total number of protons and electrons in the atom.
physics.optionD: total number of protons and neutrons in nucleus.
physics.explanation: The atomic number Z equals the number of protons in the nucleus. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: In the energy-band diagram of n-type Si, the gap between the bottom of the conduction band EC and the donor energy level ED is of the order of:
physics.explanation: The donor level ED lies just below the conduction band; EC − ED is very small, of the order of 0.01 eV (about 0.05 eV for Si). (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Two nuclei have their mass numbers in the ratio of 8 : 1. The ratio of their nuclear densities is:
physics.explanation: Nuclear density is independent of mass number, so the ratio is 1:1. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Which of the following pairs of media has the least value of critical angle?
physics.explanation: sin C = n2/n1 is smallest for the largest refractive-index ratio — diamond (2.42) to air (1.0). (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A bar magnet is dropped in a hollow metallic cylinder along its vertical axis. The acceleration of the falling magnet will be:
physics.explanation: Eddy currents induced in the metallic cylinder oppose the motion of the magnet, so its acceleration is less than g. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Which one of the following is not a scalar quantity?
physics.explanation: Electric field is a vector quantity. Voltage, resistivity and power are scalars. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: The current density due to drift of electrons in a conductor is given by : (symbols have their usual meanings) n A vd
physics.explanation: j = I/A = neAvd/A = nevd. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A particle of mass m and charge q moving with a uniform velocity v = v0x î + v0y ĵ enters a region with a magnetic field B = B0 ĵ. After some time, an electric field E = E0 ĵ is also switched on in the region. The resulting path described by the particle will be:
physics.explanation: The velocity component along B (y) is unaffected by B and gives a helix about the y-axis. An E-field along y then accelerates the particle along y, so the pitch keeps increasing. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: An inductor, a capacitor and a resistor are connected in series across an ac source of voltage. If the frequency of the source is decreased gradually, the reactance of:
physics.optionA: both the inductor and the capacitor decreases.
physics.optionB: inductor decreases and the capacitor increases.
physics.optionC: both the inductor and the capacitor increases.
physics.optionD: inductor increases and the capacitor decreases.
physics.explanation: XL = ωL decreases and XC = 1/(ωC) increases as frequency decreases. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: The electromagnetic radiations used to kill germs in water purifiers are called:
physics.explanation: UV rays are used to kill germs in water purifiers. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: In the wave picture of light, the intensity I of light is related to the amplitude A of the wave as:
physics.explanation: In the wave picture, intensity is proportional to the square of the amplitude: I ∝ A². (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: In a single-slit diffraction experiment, the width of the slit is halved. The width of the central maximum, in the diffraction pattern, will become:
physics.explanation: Width of the central maximum = 2λD/a, so halving the slit width a doubles it. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
physics.questionText: A graph is plotted between the stopping potential (on y-axis) and the frequency of incident radiation (on x-axis) for a metal. The product of the slope of the straight line obtained and the magnitude of charge on an electron is equal to:
physics.explanation: eV0 = hν − φ0, so the slope of V0 vs ν is h/e. Slope × e = h. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
physics.questionText: Light of frequency 6.4 × 10¹⁴ Hz is incident on a metal of work function 2.14 eV. The maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electrons is about:

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: If a p-n junction diode is reverse biased,
physics.optionD: the current is mainly due to majority carriers.
physics.explanation: Reverse bias adds to the built-in potential, so the potential barrier is raised; the small current is due to minority carriers. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText:
Assertion (A): The internal resistance of a cell is constant.
Reason (R): Ionic concentration of the electrolyte remains same during use of a cell.
physics.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
physics.optionD: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
physics.explanation: Both statements are false. Internal resistance depends on the electrolyte's concentration and temperature and changes as the cell is used. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText:
Assertion (A): When the radius of a circular loop carrying a steady current is doubled, its magnetic moment becomes four times.
Reason (R): The magnetic moment of a circular loop carrying a steady current is proportional to the area of the loop.
physics.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
physics.optionD: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
physics.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: m = IA = Iπr², so doubling r makes m four times. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: At 0 K, the resistivity of an intrinsic semiconductor is:
physics.explanation: At 0 K there are no free charge carriers, so the semiconductor behaves as an insulator with infinite resistivity. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
physics.questionText: In an experiment on photoelectric effect, the intensity of incident radiation is increased, keeping the frequency v the same. The number of photoelectrons emitted will:
physics.explanation: Higher intensity at the same frequency means more photons per second, so more photoelectrons are emitted. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: The SI unit of mobility of charge carriers is:
physics.explanation: Mobility μ = vd/E has units (m/s)/(V/m) = m² V⁻¹ s⁻¹. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: In a moving coil galvanometer, the deflecting torque τ acting on the coil is related to the current I flowing through it as:
physics.explanation: Deflecting torque τ = NIAB, which is directly proportional to I. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Electromagnetic waves of wavelength of the order of a few meters were first produced and detected in the laboratory by:
physics.explanation: Hertz (1887) first produced and detected EM waves of wavelength of a few metres in the laboratory. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: The emf and internal resistance of a cell are E and r respectively. It is connected across an external resistance R = 2r. The potential drop across the terminals of the cell will be : E E
physics.explanation: I = E/(R + r) = E/3r, so terminal voltage V = IR = 2E/3. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A battery of emf E and internal resistance r is connected to an external circuit. The potential drop within the battery is proportional to:
physics.explanation: The potential drop inside the battery is Ir, which is proportional to the current. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
physics.questionText: The momentum of a photon of wavelength λ is:
physics.explanation: The momentum of a photon is p = h/λ. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Two wires of equal length and radii r and 2r are connected in series. Their resistivities are 2ρ and ρ respectively. For the same current passing through the combination, the potential drops across their ends will be in the ratio:
physics.explanation: R = ρL/(πr²): R1 ∝ 2ρ/r² and R2 ∝ ρ/(4r²), so R1 : R2 = 8 : 1. With the same current, V1 : V2 = 8 : 1. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A capacitor is charged by a battery. Between the plates, during process of charging:
physics.optionC: both displacement current and conduction current exist.
physics.explanation: No charge crosses the gap between the plates; the changing electric field there constitutes only displacement current. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: For the forward biasing of a p-n junction diode, which of the following statements is not correct?
physics.optionD: Forward current is due to the diffusion of both holes and electrons.
physics.explanation: In forward bias the depletion layer becomes narrower; it does not widen. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Two cells, each of emf E, with internal resistances r and 2r are connected in parallel. The equivalent emf of the combination is:
physics.explanation: Eeq = (E/r + E/2r)/(1/r + 1/2r) = E. Identical emfs in parallel give the same emf. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Two charges q1 and q2 are placed at the centres of two (uncharged) spherical conducting shells of radii r1 and r2 respectively. The shells are arranged such that their centres are d [> (r1 + r2)] apart. The force on q2 due to q1 is:
physics.explanation: q1 at the centre of its (uncharged) conducting shell induces charges whose net effect outside is the same as a point charge q1 at the centre. So the force on q2 is (1/4πε0)q1q2/d². (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: An electron enters a uniform magnetic field with speed v. It describes a semicircular path and comes out of the field. The final speed of the electron is : v
physics.explanation: The magnetic force is perpendicular to velocity and does no work, so the speed stays v. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: The electromagnetic waves used in radar systems are:
physics.explanation: Microwaves are used in radar systems. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Which of the following statements is not true for nuclear forces?
physics.optionA: They are stronger than Coulomb forces.
physics.optionB: They have about the same magnitude for different pairs of nucleons.
physics.optionD: They saturate as the separation between two nucleons increases.
physics.explanation: The nuclear force is attractive at normal separations but strongly repulsive below about 0.8 fm, so it is not always attractive. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: An ac voltage v = v0 sin ωt is applied to a series combination of a resistor R and an element X. The instantaneous current in the circuit is I = I0 sin(ωt + π/4). Then which of the following is correct?
physics.optionA: X is a capacitor and XC = √2 R
physics.optionB: X is an inductor and XL = R
physics.optionC: X is an inductor and XL = √2 R
physics.optionD: X is a capacitor and XC = R
physics.explanation: Current leads voltage by π/4, so X is a capacitor with tan φ = XC/R = 1, i.e. XC = R. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A plane wavefront is incident on a concave mirror of radius of curvature R. The radius of the reflected wavefront will be:
physics.explanation: A concave mirror converts a plane wavefront into a spherical wavefront converging at the focus, so its radius is f = R/2. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
physics.questionText: A proton and an alpha particle have the same kinetic energy. The ratio of de Broglie wavelengths associated with the proton to that with the alpha particle is:
physics.explanation: λ = h/√(2mK). With equal K, λp/λα = √(mα/mp) = √4 = 2. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: The difference between the mass of a nucleus of mass number 7 and the total mass of its constituent nucleons is 21.00 u. The binding energy per nucleon for this nucleus is equal to the energy equivalent of:
physics.explanation: Mass defect = 21 u for 7 nucleons, so binding energy per nucleon ≡ 21/7 = 3 u. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText:
Assertion (A): When three electric bulbs of power 200 W, 100 W and 50 W are connected in series to a source, the power consumed by the 50 W bulb is maximum.
Reason (R): In a series circuit, current is the same through each bulb, but the potential difference across each bulb is different.
physics.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
physics.optionD: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
physics.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: in series the current is the same, so P = I²R. The 50 W bulb has the largest resistance (R = V²/P), so it consumes the most power. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText:
Assertion (A): A current carrying square loop made of a wire of length L is placed in a magnetic field. It experiences a torque which is greater than the torque on a circular loop made of the same wire carrying the same current in the same magnetic field.
Reason (R): A square loop occupies more area than a circular loop, both made of wire of the same length.
physics.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
physics.optionD: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
physics.explanation: Both statements are false. For a fixed wire length, a circle encloses more area than a square, so the circular loop has the larger magnetic moment and torque. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A point charge q is kept at a distance r from an infinitely long straight wire with linear charge density λ. The magnitude of the electrostatic force experienced by charge q is:
physics.explanation: The field of an infinite line charge is E = λ/(2πε0r), so F = qλ/(2πε0r). (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Which one of the following has negative value of susceptibility?
physics.explanation: Lead is diamagnetic, with negative susceptibility. Al is paramagnetic, and Ni and Fe are ferromagnetic. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
physics.questionText: A light of frequency v is incident on a metal surface whose work function is W0. The kinetic energy of emitted electron is K. If the frequency of the incident light is doubled then the kinetic energy of emitted electron will be:
physics.explanation: K = hν − W0. With 2ν, K' = 2hν − W0 = 2K + W0, which is more than 2K. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Which one of the following has relative magnetic permeability between 0 and 1?
physics.explanation: Diamagnetic substances such as water have 0 < μr < 1. Al and Na are paramagnetic, and Alnico is ferromagnetic. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2023)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A thin plastic rod is bent into a circular ring of radius R. It is uniformly charged with linear charge density λ. The magnitude of the electric field at its centre is:
physics.explanation: By symmetry, the fields of diametrically opposite elements of a uniformly charged ring cancel at its centre, so E = 0. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2024)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A loop carrying a current I clockwise (as seen from above) is placed in the x-y plane in a uniform magnetic field directed along the +z axis. The tendency of the loop will be to:
