physics.explanation: Light escapes within a cone of half-angle C, where sin C = 1/n. Radius r = H tan C = H/√(n² − 1), so area = πH²/(n² − 1). (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2025)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
physics.questionText: Ina photoelectric experiment with a material of work function 2.1 eV, the stopping potential is found to be 2.5 V. The maximum kinetic energy of ejected photoelectrons is
physics.explanation: Kmax = eV0 = 2.5 eV. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2025)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Two charges —q each are placed at the vertices A and B of an equilateral triangle ABC. If M is the mid-point of AB, the net electric field at C will point along
physics.explanation: Each −q pulls the field at C towards itself (along CA and CB). The horizontal components cancel, and the resultant points along CM, towards the midpoint of AB. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2025)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A student has three resistors, each of resistance R. To obtain a resistance of 3R, she should connect:
physics.optionA: all the three resistors in series.
physics.optionB: all the three resistors in parallel.
physics.optionC: two resistors in series and then this combination in parallel with the third resistor.
physics.optionD: two resistors in parallel and then this combination in series with the third resistor.
physics.explanation: Three resistors of R in series give 3R. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2025)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: The magnetic field due to a small magnetic dipole of dipole moment ‘M’ at a distance ‘r’ from the centre along the axis of the dipole is given by Ho 2M Ho M
physics.explanation: On the axis of a short magnetic dipole, B = (μ0/4π)(2M/r³). (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2025)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A transformer is connected to a 200 V ac source. The transformer supplies 3000 V to a device. If the number of turns in the primary coil is 450, the number of turns in its secondary coil is:
physics.explanation: Ns = Np(Vs/Vp) = 450 × 3000/200 = 6750. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2025)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct ? Electric field due to static charges is
physics.optionA: conservative and field lines do not form closed loops.
physics.optionB: conservative and field lines form closed loops.
physics.optionC: non-conservative and field lines do not form closed loops.
physics.optionD: non-conservative and field lines form closed loops.
physics.explanation: The electrostatic field is conservative, and its field lines start and end on charges, so they never form closed loops. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2025)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A tub is filled with a transparent liquid to a height of 30.0 cm. The apparent depth of a coin lying at the bottom of the tub is found to be 16.0 cm. The speed of light in the liquid will be:
physics.explanation: n = real depth/apparent depth = 30/16 = 1.875, so v = c/n = 1.6 × 10⁸ m/s. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2025)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
physics.questionText: Atomic spectral emission lines of hydrogen are incident on a zinc surface. The lines which can emit photoelectrons from the surface are members of the:
physics.optionD: Neither Balmer, nor Paschen nor Lyman series |
physics.explanation: Zinc's work function is about 4.3 eV. Only Lyman lines (≥ 10.2 eV) have enough photon energy; Balmer (≤ 3.4 eV) and Paschen do not. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2025)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: The energy of an electron in a hydrogen atom in ground state is —13.6 eV. Its energy in an orbit corresponding to quantum number n is —0.544 eV. The value of n is
physics.explanation: −13.6/n² = −0.544 gives n² = 25, so n = 5. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2025)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText:
Assertion (A): In a semiconductor diode the thickness of depletion layer is not fixed.
Reason (R): Thickness of depletion layer in a semiconductor device depends upon many factors such as biasing of the semiconductor.
physics.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
physics.optionD: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
physics.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: depletion layer thickness changes with biasing (narrower in forward, wider in reverse bias). (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2025)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText:
Assertion (A): In the Bohr model of the hydrogen atom, the angular momentum of an electron in the nth orbit is proportional to the square root of its orbit radius rn.
Reason (R): According to the Bohr model, an electron can jump to its nearest orbits only.
physics.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
physics.optionD: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
physics.explanation: The assertion is true: L = nh/2π ∝ n and r ∝ n², so L ∝ √r. The reason is false: an electron can jump between any allowed orbits, not just neighbouring ones. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2025)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText:
Assertion (A): Out of Infrared and radio waves, the radio waves show more diffraction effect.
Reason (R): Radio waves have greater frequency than infrared waves.
physics.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
physics.optionD: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
physics.explanation: The assertion is true: radio waves (longer wavelength) diffract more. The reason is false: radio waves have a lower frequency than infrared. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2025)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText:
Assertion (A): In an ideal step-down transformer, electrical energy is not lost.
Reason (R): In a step-down transformer, voltage decreases but the current increases.
physics.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
physics.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
physics.optionD: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
physics.explanation: Both statements are true, but the reason does not explain the assertion. An ideal transformer loses no energy (VpIp = VsIs); that voltage falls while current rises is a consequence, not the explanation. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2025)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Two identical point charges are placed at two vertices A and B of an equilateral triangle of side l. The magnitude of the electric field at the third vertex P is E. If a hollow conducting sphere of radius l/4 is placed with its centre at P, the magnitude of the electric field at point P now becomes:
physics.explanation: The electric field inside a hollow conductor is zero, so the field at P inside the sphere becomes zero. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2025)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A battery of emf 12 V and internal resistance 0.5 Ω is connected to a 9.5 Ω resistor through a key. The ratio of the potential difference between the two terminals of the battery when the key is open to that when the key is closed is:
physics.explanation: With the key open, V = E = 12 V. With it closed, I = 12/10 = 1.2 A and V = 12 − 0.6 = 11.4 V. Ratio = 12/11.4 ≈ 1.05. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2025)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A diamagnetic substance is brought, one by one, near the north pole and the south pole of a bar magnet. It is
physics.optionA: repelled by north pole and attracted by south pole.
physics.optionB: attracted by north pole and repelled by south pole.
physics.optionC: attracted by north pole as well as by south pole.
physics.optionD: repelled by north pole as well as by south pole. |
physics.explanation: A diamagnetic substance is repelled by both poles of a magnet. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2025)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Two long solenoids of radii r1 and r2 (r2 > r1) and numbers of turns per unit length n1 and n2 respectively are co-axially wrapped one over the other. The ratio of the self-inductance of the inner solenoid to their mutual inductance is:
physics.explanation: L1 = μ0n1²πr1²l and M = μ0n1n2πr1²l (flux through the inner solenoid), so L1/M = n1/n2. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2025)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A coil of an ac generator, having 100 turns each of area 0.1 m², rotates at half a rotation per second in a magnetic field of 0.02 T. The maximum emf generated in the coil is:

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: The focal length of a concave mirror in air is f. When the mirror is immersed in a liquid of refractive index 5/3, its focal length will become:
physics.explanation: A mirror's focal length (R/2) depends only on its geometry, not on the surrounding medium, so it stays f. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2025)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: When the resistance measured between p and n ends of a p-n junction diode is high, it can act as a/an —
physics.explanation: A diode with high resistance in one direction and low in the other can act as a switch (OFF in reverse bias). (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2025)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: Consider two identical dipoles D1 and D2. Charges −q and q of dipole D1 are located at (0, 0) and (a, 0), and those of dipole D2 at (0, a) and (0, 2a) in the x-y plane respectively. The net dipole moment of the system is:
physics.explanation: D1: −q at (0,0), q at (a,0) gives p1 = qa î. D2: −q at (0,a), q at (0,2a) gives p2 = qa ĵ. The net dipole moment is qa(î + ĵ). (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2025)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: A material is pushed out when placed in a uniform magnetic field. The material is
physics.explanation: Diamagnetic materials are pushed out of (expelled from) a magnetic field. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2025)

physics.subject: Physics
physics.questionText: The plane face of a planoconvex lens is silvered. The refractive index of material and radius of curvature of the curved surface of the lens are n and R respectively. This lens will behave as a concave mirror of focal length 1 R R (A) = ®) Gp R (C) nR (D) 2(n- 1)
physics.explanation: A silvered plano-convex lens acts as a mirror of power P = 2P_lens + P_plane mirror = 2(n−1)/R. So f = R/[2(n−1)]. (CBSE Class 12 Physics 2025)
